factorRatings.note: The Infatuation, Seattle Met, and Tasting Table all single out the Detroit-style square pies -- chewy, focaccia-like crust with frizzled cheese edges -- alongside wood-fired round pies; opened in North Ballard in April 2020.

West Seattle Herald's 2018 launch profile describes a thin, crisp crust made with Mantako flour and Grande mozzarella and scratch-made, locally sourced ingredients; Intentionalist's neighborhood guide calls it among the best pizza regulars have had outside the East Coast.

The Infatuation calls its New York-style slices 'greasy-in-a-good-way' and recommends it mainly as a reliable late-night stop with an open booth past midnight; Intentionalist notes the bar-and-slice shop has operated since 1998.

Hoodline's 2018 opening profile describes thin, crispy-crust pizzas made with ingredients sourced from Italy and the owner's own Oregon farm, including seasonal pies like the Autunno (gorgonzola, apple, walnut, honey) and the Calabrian-chile Piccante.
